description: Decoded pre-execution briefs for the queued timelock operations on the radar: scheduling logs, decoded calls, current vs new state, verified sources, risk notes and cast reproduction commands. Every value was read at the pinned finalized block on two independent public RPC endpoints that agreed (captures/decode-*.json). The Compound V3 brief's Linea-side values were read at a Linea finalized block on two independent Linea endpoints.

operations.label: AssetRouter upgrade adding a fixed deposit fee
BTC.b token upgrade that charges the deposit fee on mint
LBTC token upgrade; unpausing transfers moves to the manager role

risk_notes: The three operations are independent (predecessor 0x0, same ETA 2026-11-17 18:29:47 UTC); any executor may run them in any order. The new BTC.b implementation reads AssetRouter.depositFee() on every proof mint, and the current AssetRouter implementation has no such function (the call reverts at the pinned block): if the BTC.b upgrade executes before the AssetRouter upgrade, BTC.b proof mints revert until the router is upgraded.

No initializer runs (upgradeAndCall with empty data). Every per-token deposit fee starts at 0, so nothing is charged on execution. The minimum stays 2,000 sats (0.00002 BTC): the storage field is renamed minRequestAmount (oz-renamed-from), and non-BTC redeems are now held to it too.

After the upgrade a non-zero fee is split off every proof mint and minted to the token treasury. OPERATOR_ROLE can set it to 100-1,000 sats per mint without the timelock. Any other value needs DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (the timelock), and the fee is capped at half the minimum.

BaseLBTC.unpauseTransfers moves from DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (the 1-day timelock) to MANAGER_ROLE, the role that already clears the mint/burn pause: resuming paused transfers no longer waits for the timelock.

All three were scheduled in one Safe transaction (0xf18a01875814c62d83b089f6565c9e02a80c296fdb81306d04d44f11e795ae05) sent to 0x251a604e8e8f6906d60f8dedc5aaeb8cd38f4892, the same Safe that BTC.b and LBTC name as treasury: the deposit-fee recipient after the upgrade.

AssetRouter.changeNativeToken no longer deletes the previous native token's route. Storage stays append-only: TokenConfig gains depositFee at the end of a mapped struct, and AssetRouterStorage appends maxDepositFee + feeTokens in its ERC-7201 namespace. OpenZeppelin libraries are bumped in all three implementations.

beaconOwnerOwner.kind: a timelock with a 21,600 s delay

risk_notes: setDeviation(25) widens the strategy's calm check from 9 to 25 ticks: how far the current pool tick may sit from its 120 s TWAP before the strategy refuses to act. The pool's tick spacing is 50. This is a looser price-manipulation guard on the USDC-VVV pool, not a code change.
At the pinned block isCalm() = true, with the tick (246,120) 1 ticks from the TWAP (246,121). The flag moves with price; after execution, moves of up to 25 ticks from the TWAP still count as calm.

The strategy is a beacon proxy. Its implementation (0xde4e9b0e287c38d0a8cc53ade899edb159827bf1) is not verified on Sourcify, though setDeviation, maxTickDeviation and isCalm are confirmed in its dispatch table. The beacon (0x883dda584b6d4367a26f897d7bfc3e6f5dd9c7a1) is controlled through Beefy's StrategyFactory (verified on Sourcify), which this timelock owns: implementation swaps also wait for the 21,600 s delay.
This is not a strategy upgrade: the selector is setDeviation(int56), not upgradeStrat(), and the vault keeps the same strategy.

risk_notes: One scheduleBatch of 5 setManageRoot(address,bytes32) calls (selector 0x21801a99): 2 on the liquidUSD manager, 2 on the liquidETH manager, 1 on the liquidBTC manager. Every call replaces a non-zero root that is live at the pin.

A manage root is the Merkle root of the calls a strategist may make through the vault. The leaves of the queued roots are not onchain: what each strategist can do after execution cannot be read from this operation alone.
liquidETH: the queued root for 0xc811…23a2 goes to an externally owned account (no code at the pin), so a single key will be able to run every call that root allows.
liquidUSD: the root kept for the manager's own address (0x7b57…c13c) is set to zero, so manage calls that the manager contract itself submits can no longer pass Merkle verification.

The 4-of-6 Safe 0xcea8…ec96 (Safe 1.3.0) that scheduled the batch is this timelock's proposer, canceller and executor; the executor role is not open, so only that Safe can execute after the ETA or cancel before it.
On all three managers owner() is the zero address and each manager's authority lets this timelock call setManageRoot (canCall = true at the pin): execution needs no other approval.

sourceDiff.storage: append-only: IEigenServiceManager.EigenServiceManagerStorage (ERC-7201 namespace) gains pendingSlashes at the end; ReentrancyGuardTransient uses transient storage (no persistent slot)

slash.before: clears the slashed EigenLayer shares in the same call and transfers the collateral to the recipient (Slash event)
slash.after: records PendingSlash(recipient, amount valued at slash time) and emits SlashQueued; the collateral moves only in completeSlash

behaviour.completeSlash: permissionless; reverts until EigenLayer's slash resolution delay has passed or while EigenLayer is paused; pays min(pending amount, collateral available)
behaviour.distributeRewards: reverts with InvalidRewardToken for any token other than USDC (0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48)
behaviour.registerStrategy: reverts with InvalidCollateral when the strategy's underlying token is USDC
behaviour.delegationDistributeRewards: Delegation.distributeRewards(agent, asset) is permissionless, takes any asset and calls the agent network's distributeRewards(agent, asset)

risk_notes: Slashing becomes two-step. Today slash() clears the operator's slashed EigenLayer shares and pays the collateral to the recipient in the same call. After the upgrade slash() only records a PendingSlash (recipient and the amount valued at slash time) and emits SlashQueued; the collateral reaches the recipient when anyone calls completeSlash(operator, slashId) after EigenLayer's slash resolution delay, and it reverts until then or while EigenLayer is paused.

The payout is min(amount valued at slash time, collateral this contract actually received). The source reasons that the strategy share price cannot fall before the shares are cleared, so the recipient is not short-paid; any surplus stays in the service manager.

Who can slash is unchanged: the slash role on this contract is held only by Cap's Delegation contract (0xF3E3Eae671000612CE3Fd15e1019154C1a4d693F) at the pin. A liquidation that slashes an EigenLayer-backed agent now delivers its collateral to the liquidator later, not in the liquidation transaction.

Rewards become USDC-only: distributeRewards reverts for any other token, and registerStrategy refuses a USDC collateral strategy. Delegation.distributeRewards(agent, asset) is permissionless and forwards any asset to the agent's network, so for an agent on this network it now reverts unless the asset is USDC.

No initializer runs (upgradeToAndCall with empty data). Storage is append-only: pendingSlashes is added at the end of the ERC-7201 EigenServiceManager storage struct, and the reentrancy guard on completeSlash uses transient storage.

Upgrades of this proxy are authorised only through Cap's AccessControl role bytes4(0) on this contract, whose only member at the pin is this 1-day timelock. The operation was scheduled from Cap's Developer Safe (proposer) with predecessor 0x0.

risk_notes: This is not a Base operation: the target is Linea's L1 MessageService (LineaRollup), and the message goes to Compound's LineaBridgeReceiver on Linea, which accepts it only from this Ethereum Timelock (govTimelock).

The whole reserve balance moves: Compound WETH (cWETHv3) on Linea held 25.942056261701576527 WETH of reserves at the Linea pin, exactly the 25.942056261701576527 WETH that withdrawReserves requests. Reserves only change with market activity (no borrows at the pin), so a lower balance at execution would make withdrawReserves revert on Linea.

Two delays stack: the 2-day Ethereum Timelock (ETA 2026-11-20 18:58:23 UTC), then the receiver queues the three Linea calls behind the 1-day Linea Timelock, executable by anyone via executeProposal within its 14-day grace period.

The L2 message sends 25.952056261701576527 ETH: the 25.942056261701576527 ETH unwrapped plus the 0.01 ETH fee. The Linea Timelock held 0.016655898522808438 ETH of its own at the pin, enough for the fee; with less, the third call reverts. The ETH reaches the Ethereum Timelock only after the Linea-to-Ethereum message is claimed on L1.
The Ethereum-side message prepays no fee (_fee = 0) and no value: delivery on Linea follows Linea's message-service claiming rules.

Proposal 625 was queued by CompoundGovernor (the Timelock's admin) at block 26,443,894; anyone may execute it from the ETA for the 14-day grace period. The radar reads queuedTransactions(txHash) and the Timelock's ExecuteTransaction / CancelTransaction logs.

risk_notes: After execution any one of the 15 signers of the Safe 0xEEfebb1546d88EA0909435DF6f615084DD3c5Bd8 (threshold 1) can call pause() on each of the four liquidators. While a liquidator is paused, its whenNotPaused entry points revert: on Liquidator and BrokerLiquidator every BOT liquidation, smart-collateral and token-sale function; on V3Liquidator liquidations, V3 share redemption and token sales; on PublicLiquidator the four public liquidation functions (redeemSmartCollateral stays callable there). withdraw functions and admin setters are not gated.

unpause() needs MANAGER on each liquidator. At the pin MANAGER is held by the 3-of-6 Safe 0x8d388136d578dCD791D081c6042284CED6d9B0c6 and by Lista's MarketFactory proxy 0xA2ff080D4c0b71B6c8796129DD4aCc0B09D7592c; the batch adds the EmergencySwitchHub. Pausing takes one signature, resuming takes the 3-of-6 Safe or a contract.

The EmergencySwitchHub 0xBafB0B5B70A9844Fb9F132ba1C28F888Dd113B34 (Sourcify-verified EmergencySwitchHub) lets its PAUSER call pauseAll / pauseContracts and its MANAGER call unpauseAll and addPausableContracts. Its PAUSER is the same 1-of-15 Safe, its MANAGER the 3-of-6 Safe, and the hub's PAUSER role admin is MANAGER: the 3-of-6 Safe can add hub pausers without this timelock. At the pin none of the four liquidators is in getPausableContracts() (12 entries), so the hub reaches them only after its MANAGER adds them.
On the liquidators themselves, PAUSER and MANAGER are administered by DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, which this timelock holds: further grants there still wait the 1-day delay.

No initializer runs (upgradeToAndCall with empty data). Each queued implementation only adds OpenZeppelin PausableUpgradeable (ERC-7201 namespaced flag), the PAUSER constant, pause() / unpause() and whenNotPaused on the entry points above; the Sourcify storage layouts are identical, so the proxies start unpaused. The other changed files only add interface declarations.

All four queued implementations are Sourcify exact matches (verified 2026-11-17). The batch was scheduled by the 3-of-6 Safe 0x08aE09467ff962aF105c23775B9Bc8EAa175D27F, which is this timelock's proposer, canceller and executor; the executor role is not open to everyone.
